events.continuity_hook: Starts a new municipal startup trip after the Palm Springs weekend is booked and the spring client-site calendar picks back up.
events.interaction_goal: Build a flight, rental-car, and hotel shortlist that protects the Tuesday gate time while leaving room for the possible Wednesday controls review.
events.scenario_brief: A Southern Arizona water authority asks Jonah to be onsite for a PFAS pilot skid startup, with a Tuesday 7:15 a.m. security check and a Wednesday afternoon controls review if the integrator finishes wiring. He needs Monday Bay Area-to-Tucson options compared with a Phoenix nonstop plus the longer drive, including rental-car pickup time, a stop to verify the sampling kit, and enough rest before the early gate. Hotel options should favor a well-reviewed property closer to the plant with parking, practical dinner access, and in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge if available; unresolved items are whether the carbon media delivery clears the plant Monday and whether the Wednesday controls review stays on the schedule.

events.continuity_hook: Refines the Tucson startup plan once the media delivery is confirmed and the second workday extends into Thursday.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the stronger outbound airport plan, confirm the hotel direction, and identify a Thursday return window that does not rush the controls review.
events.scenario_brief: The plant confirms the carbon media delivery, but the integrator shifts the controls review to Thursday morning and asks Jonah to plan for a longer Wednesday sampling day. He wants to narrow between a Monday afternoon one-stop into Tucson that lands before dinner and a later Phoenix nonstop that looks cleaner on paper but adds a nighttime drive. The plant-side hotel still looks like the better operational fit if the room amenities and breakfast timing check out; the remaining decision is whether Thursday return travel can work after the revised controls review.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Tucson PFAS startup trip from comparison to booked itinerary after the Thursday meeting time settles.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize flights, rental car, hotel reservation, room notes, seat choices, and the Tuesday-through-Thursday site schedule.
events.scenario_brief: The controls review is locked for Thursday 10:00 a.m. to noon, and the sampling kit will be held at the contractor trailer. Jonah books the Monday afternoon one-stop into Tucson because it avoids the late Phoenix drive, adds a compact SUV, and reserves the well-rated plant-area hotel with parking, breakfast, restaurant access nearby, and a coffee maker and mini-fridge request. The return is set for Thursday late afternoon with one comfortable connection back to the Bay Area, and window seats are selected where available; the only remaining check is whether the utility or contractor issues his visitor badge.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a conference-planning episode after the Tucson client-site visit is settled.
events.interaction_goal: Create a concise flight and hotel comparison around booth check-in, the Wednesday session, hotel quality, walkability, and the possible Thursday evening commitment.
events.scenario_brief: Jonah is assigned to cover a regional water-operations expo in Portland, with Monday evening booth material check-in, a Wednesday 9:00 a.m. technical session, and a possible Thursday customer dinner. He needs Bay Area-to-Portland flight options for Monday afternoon, plus a comparison between the official convention hotel block and a better-rated nearby property that is a few blocks farther from the expo hall. He likely will not need a rental car if transit and rideshare timing work; unresolved items are whether he must stay for Thursday booth teardown and whether the customer dinner becomes mandatory.

events.continuity_hook: Refines the Portland expo plan once the session time moves earlier and the customer dinner becomes firm.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the outbound flight, hotel choice, and return-day plan before the hotel block deadline passes.
events.scenario_brief: The expo organizer moves Jonah's technical session to Wednesday 7:45 a.m., and the distributor confirms the Thursday customer dinner near the waterfront. The official hotel block is close to the hall but still shows uneven guest feedback, while the nearby independent hotel has stronger reviews, a quieter-room option, and better evening restaurant access. Jonah wants to narrow between a Monday afternoon nonstop on a non-United carrier and a United one-stop that arrives later; the unresolved issue is whether a teammate can take Thursday booth teardown so Jonah can return Friday morning instead of late Thursday night.

events.continuity_hook: Finalizes the Portland expo travel after teardown coverage and the return morning are confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Book the flights and hotel, add room notes, confirm no rental car is needed, choose seats, and summarize the expo commitments.
events.scenario_brief: A teammate agrees to handle Thursday booth teardown, so Jonah only needs to stay through the customer dinner and can fly back Friday morning. He books the Monday afternoon nonstop into Portland because it gives the cleanest arrival before booth material check-in, reserves the better-rated hotel near the convention center with a quiet-room note and in-room fridge request, and skips the rental car in favor of transit and rideshares. The return is set for Friday morning after breakfast, with seats selected and the conference agenda reduced to booth coverage, the early technical session, and the Thursday dinner.
